correctness.rationale: The column marginal ranges over exactly the nodally nonnegative polynomial samples: necessity follows by summing rows and sufficiency by assigning the marginal divided by N_x to every row. The normalized slice is a compact convex subset of the probability simplex. The affine constraints are a >= |b| and the moments are na and n mu_n b. The quadratic normalized slice is a polygon: a vertex must have two distinct active nodes by injectivity of evaluation, and two active nodes fix a ray. An upward quadratic with two roots is nonnegative at every node iff the roots are adjacent; a downward one requires the two endpoints. The resulting mean is -2 mu_n c/(mu_n+c^2-delta_n^2) for signed midpoint c, or zero on the downward ray. This gives both endpoints and every intervening value by mixing. The first adjacent pair gives a strictly larger bound than mu_n since mu_n<1. The midpoints become dense and the envelope converges uniformly to 2c/(1+3c^2), maximized at c=1/sqrt(3). R_2=1 at n=3, but for n>=4 every nonzero polynomial of degree <=2 has support on at least two nodes, so by compactness R_2<1. Moving a mass t from a lower occupied node to velocity 1 increases momentum by t(1-v_k) at unchanged mass, with Frobenius distance at most sqrt(2/N_x)t. The QP objective is coercive and strictly convex in the core; the feasible set is closed convex. This is nonnegativity, not strict positivity at the frontier.
